prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
The FOURTH attached image is the EDIT TARGET: an eight-frame blue fish swim sheet. Images 1 and 2 are approved Daoist Q HD hand-painted finish references. Image 3 is the fish identity master. Preserve that fish identity, all eight distinct tail/fin poses from image 4, their row-major animation phase, cyan/cobalt scales and gold-outlined translucent membranes. Correct ONLY the framing and cell separation.
CRITICAL edit: the current eight fish are much too large and touch their cell borders. Recompose the sheet as EXACTLY four columns by two rows of equal SQUARE cells on a true transparent background, native wide 2:1 ratio. Shrink the entire artwork of EACH FISH to only SIXTY PERCENT of its cell width, preserving its own anatomy, all fine fin tips and aspect ratio. Put its overall artwork center exactly at each cell center. This creates AT LEAST TWENTY PERCENT blank transparent padding on the left AND right of each cell, with ample top/bottom blank space as well. Keep all eight fish the SAME scale. Each complete fish is visually isolated by very wide blank gutters. Nothing crosses or approaches a cell border.
Retain actual differing tail/fin articulation in each of the eight frames, not eight repeated static copies: tail-neutral, upper half, upper peak, upper recovery, neutral opposite direction, lower half, lower peak, lower recovery; paired fins opposed. Keep eye/mouth/head shape, front-body orientation and marking layout stable across frames. Each fish faces RIGHT, fixed camera. No whole-sprite rotation/zoom/drift as fake movement. Keep the polished detailed gold trim and cyan-blue hand-painted fish design from the fish master. Remove incidental isolated color flecks surrounding fish so the edges are clean alpha; retain normal soft antialiasing. Genuine transparent RGBA, no painted checkerboard, no background, no UI, no grid lines, no text, no numbers, no extra objects. Do not enlarge fish to fill blank space: wide transparent gutters are required for game slicing.
